Macron targets Trump over French riots
French President Emmanuel Macron has slammed as “stupid” and “unacceptable” remarks by foreign leaders about the unrest gripping France, in an apparent swipe at US President Donald Trump, who blamed the violence on Paris’ lax border policies.
France has been rocked by some of its worst riots in years, sparked last month by teacher shortages and crumbling schools before escalating into nationwide protests over inequality, soaring living costs and public service cuts.
Hundreds of thousands took to the streets over the weekend as demonstrations descended into clashes with police, arson and looting. Nearly 2,400 people were arrested, around 1,000 officers injured, hundreds of businesses looted and buildings torched, with damage estimated at “hundreds of millions of euros.”
Trump pours fuel on the fire
Trump claimed that “migrants, jihadists, and communists” had “conquered, looted, and burned” France, accusing Macron of failing to secure its borders. He urged European leaders to “close their borders,” before seizing on the unrest to rally Republicans ahead of the November 3 midterms, warning that scenes of “burning steeples and raging fires” were “what the Radical Dumocrats want to do to AMERICA” with their own migration agenda.
Macron isn’t amused
Speaking to reporters on Wednesday, Macron accused outside actors of manipulating information about the events to their gain.
“There was foreign manipulation of information, which gave rise to unacceptable and stupid comments from many people, including foreign leaders,” he said. “We have had people claiming that we were invaded by hordes of migrants and Islamists, which is completely false… These people annoy me.”
Asked whether he was referring to Trump, Macron replied: “Among others.”
President Emmanuel Macron said Wednesday that foreign leaders — including those “on the other side of the Atlantic” — were seeking to exploit France’s tense social climate for political gain following a weekend of street violence and looting.
Protests over soaring living costs… pic.twitter.com/XlitrzVoK6
— The Associated Press (@AP) October 21, 2026
While there is no clear evidence that migrants have played a disproportionate role in the unrest, multiple videos posted online have shown protesters waving Palestinian flags alongside French ones.
They said the riots and destruction in France were about the cost of living and schools.
Then explain the Palestinian flags and keffiyehs.
Allowing mass third-world migration is why France is done. pic.twitter.com/jDr733vcOx
— TaraBull (@TaraBull) October 19, 2026
French authorities have largely blamed the violence on radical far-left groups and opportunistic criminals, without linking its organization to immigrants. Meanwhile, politicians across France’s political spectrum blamed Macron and his government for the unrest, accusing the administration of undermining public services and failing to maintain order.
Macron leaves the building
Macron made his remarks during a Middle East trip that he refused to postpone despite the turmoil at home, leaving his government to deal with the fallout. He tried to defend his decision, insisting that changing his plans would have signaled “nervousness” and that he had given his government a “sufficient roadmap.” Yet with just six months until France’s presidential election and his approval rating at a record-low 15%, the trip has only fueled perceptions of a lame-duck presidency as Macron quite literally left the scene as Paris and other cities burned.
His absence drew criticism of an “absent president” and left rivals Marine Le Pen, who leads first-round polling for April 2027 with 32-36% support, and Jean-Luc Melenchon, to dominate the debate at home.
Meanwhile, Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu has ordered curfews ahead of fresh protests, with gatherings banned near Paris landmarks including the Louvre and Champs-Elysees for three days. France also plans to deploy 1,000 counterterrorism troops to reinforce police on Saturday, October 24. Lecornu is due to meet mayors of riot-hit cities on Thursday to coordinate efforts to prevent further violence.
Russia, the usual suspect
In his remarks, Macron also dismissed suggestions of foreign interference in the unrest itself, citing a lack of evidence. His remarks followed a flurry of Western media speculation seeking to blame the riots, which spread from France to Belgium, Italy, Portugal and Albania, on outside meddling – with Russia once again cast as the usual suspect.
Outlets such as The Financial Times and the Telegraph, citing “anonymous” sources, reported that several EU governments had asked intelligence agencies to investigate possible Russian involvement. The FT expanded the suspect list to Iran and Algeria, claiming some officials had even demanded a formal EU probe.
European officials also joined the finger-pointing. Italian Defense Minister Guido Crosetto suggested the riots were part of a “hybrid war” waged through social media by an unidentified actor. Albanian Prime Minister Edi Rama went further, accusing Russian and Iranian intelligence services outright.
Yet the allegations have apparently failed to convince even Brussels. According to Euronews, the European Commission has declined to launch an investigation, citing insufficient evidence.
The speculation follows a familiar pattern of EU officials invoking “hybrid warfare” and the alleged “Russian threat” amid domestic turmoil. Just this week, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen accused Moscow and Minsk of “weaponizing migration,” linking them to the summer crisis in Spain’s Ceuta, where an estimated 70,000 migrants crossed from Morocco, sparking a border emergency and political fallout over EU migration policies. However, yet again, she presented no evidence connecting either country to the crisis.
Moscow says look closer to home
Moscow routinely dismisses allegations of interference and claims of a Russian threat as “absurd” fabrications, accusing EU leaders of using the narrative to deflect blame for their own policy failures and distract from mounting domestic crises.
Responding to Rama’s accusations, Russian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova told him to look closer to home.
“These are citizens of your own country who took to the streets to protest. Don’t shift your responsibility onto others. Deal with your own domestic problems,” she said.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov, meanwhile, described the unrest sweeping the EU as evidence of “a major crisis… bordering on chaos.”

Film about Ukrainian volunteer soldiers to be screened at Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival

Currency pressure easing on Swiss pharma giant Roche
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-22
12:37:58 UTC
21:37:58 KST

Currency pressure easing on Swiss pharma giant Roche
At Roche, the headwinds from currency fluctuations have eased somewhat after nine months. The third quarter, in particular, brought some relief thanks to a weaker Swiss franc. On Thursday, the pharmaceutical group confirmed its previous targets for the full year.
Roche generated sales of CHF46.5 billion ($56.5 billion) between January and September. In the reporting currency, the Swiss franc, this represented an increase of 1%, as Roche announced on Thursday. At constant exchange rates, the increase was 6%. The Group has therefore met its own target, which is based on constant exchange rates.
While Roche had still suffered to some extent from the strong Swiss franc in the first and second quarters, its depreciation in the third quarter provided some tailwind, which was broadly in line with analysts’ expectations. As Roche itself reports, currency effects were slightly positive in the third quarter at +1%, having previously been a clear drag at -11% in the first quarter and -4% in the second.
+ Pharma pushes for higher European drug prices, Trump or no Trump
Of the two business divisions, the larger pharmaceuticals division generated sales of CHF36.2 billion in the first three quarters, an increase of 2%. The five key growth drivers – Xolair, Hemlibra, Ocrevus, Phesgo and Vabysmo – together generated sales of CHF16.8 billion (+12%). Sales of off-patent products (Avastin, Herceptin, MabThera/Rituxan, Lucentis and Actemra/RoActemra) fell by a total of CHF600 million.
In the diagnostics business, Roche generated CHF10.3 billion, which was in line with the previous year’s figure. This indicates that the negative impact of the price reform in China has noticeably eased. Roche had repeatedly emphasised that the impact was expected to diminish as the year progressed. By way of comparison: in the first quarter, revenue had fallen by 7%, and by 3% in the first half of the year.
Roche does not traditionally report profit figures for odd-numbered quarters.
Outlook confirmed
With the figures reported, Roche has largely exceeded analysts’ estimates.
Management, led by CEO Thomas Schinecker, has confirmed its previous guidance for the rest of the financial year. At constant exchange rates, sales are expected to rise by a mid-single-digit percentage. Core earnings per share are expected to grow in the high single-digit percentage range. Furthermore, the Group remains committed to increasing the dividend in Swiss francs.

Türkiye lowers key interest rate to 36 percent after five pauses
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-22
12:37:48 UTC
21:37:48 KST

Türkiye's central bank has reduced its benchmark policy rate by 100 basis points to 36 percent, in line with market expectations, after holding rates steady for five consecutive meetings.
The bank's Monetary Policy Committee, chaired by Governor Fatih Karahan on Thursday, lowered the one-week repo auction rate from 37 percent.
It also reduced the overnight lending rate from 40 percent to 39 percent and the overnight borrowing rate from 35.5 percent to 34.5 percent.
Despite monthly fluctuations, recent inflation figures and leading indicators confirm a slowdown in the underlying inflation trend, the committee said in a statement.
Economic activity data and the limited pass-through of supply shocks to domestic prices indicate that domestic demand remains weak, it added.
However, elevated energy prices stemming from ongoing geopolitical tensions continue to pose an upside risk to the inflation outlook.
Geopolitical developments
The committee said it is closely monitoring the impact of geopolitical developments on inflation through costs, economic activity, and expectations.
“The tight monetary policy stance, which will be maintained until price stability is achieved, will strengthen the disinflation process through demand, exchange rate, and expectation channels,” it said.
Future rate decisions will take into account realised and expected inflation, as well as its underlying trend, to maintain the tightness needed to support the projected disinflation path in line with interim targets.
The size and timing of policy steps will be determined prudently on a meeting-by-meeting basis, with a focus on the inflation outlook.
“In case of a significant and persistent deterioration in the inflation outlook, monetary policy stance will be tightened,” the committee said, reiterating its attention to upside inflation risks.
Additional macroprudential measures will support monetary transmission if unexpected developments emerge in credit and deposit markets, while liquidity management tools will continue to be used effectively.

What’s the PHP coding flaw that could pull down 70 percent of the internet?
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-22
12:37:34 UTC
21:37:34 KST

What’s the PHP coding flaw that could pull down 70 percent of the internet?
The vulnerability allows a hacker to change a website or extract data, including personal information.
Government websites in Europe and elsewhere have gone offline after news of critical vulnerabilities in a widely used programming language sent website operators scrambling to protect their systems.
Developers of the PHP programming language on Wednesday released urgent new fixes, saying all users were “encouraged to update immediately”.
PHP runs on the servers that host websites, building pages behind the scenes before they reach a visitor’s browser. Most people never see it, but it powers everything from blogs to online shops and government portals.
The vulnerabilities, which had been lurking in the software for years, were uncovered with the help of artificial intelligence. Details about them leaked online on Tuesday before fixes were available, forcing PHP to rush them out.
Experts said they were bracing for a wave of intrusions as hackers jumped to get ahead of the updates.
What is the bug?
Andrew Cullen, a lecturer on AI and cybersecurity at the University of Melbourne, said many devices in the world are connected to one piece of foundational software, which is where the bug was found.
The vulnerability allows a hacker to run code on a website, meaning they could change the website or force it to release personal information collected in a database, Cullen told Al Jazeera.
Both flaws stem from how PHP handles fatal errors, such as running out of memory. Because the problem sits in PHP itself, even the simplest website running an affected version can be vulnerable, and attackers could read passwords and other credentials from a server’s memory, the cloud security company Wiz said. Both flaws scored 9.2 out of 10 on the industry’s standard severity scale, placing them in the “critical” category.
The two flaws, nicknamed PHP2Shell, were found independently by two cybersecurity companies using AI. Calif, working with OpenAI, reported the first on August 11. Wiz, which is owned by Google, reported the second on August 24.
The vulnerabilities remained hidden in the PHP codebase for more than a decade and would have been extraordinarily complicated for a human hacker to take advantage of, Wiz said in a statement.
Calif and Wiz said they had coordinated with each other, the PHP team and OpenAI before making the vulnerabilities public.
However, Amazon security chief CJ Moses said his security team detected an attempt to exploit the vulnerabilities on October 17, four days before the public disclosure.
Moses said it was unclear how the hacker learned of the flaws while Calif’s and Wiz’s reports were still under embargo. Security researchers usually keep details of flaws secret until a fix is ready, so attackers cannot use them in the meantime.
Who can potentially be affected?
PHP, a language that dates back to the early 1990s and initially stood for Personal Home Page, underpins huge parts of the public-facing web and is baked into WordPress, Drupal, Joomla and Magento sites, meaning any critical vulnerability potentially has enormous knock-on consequences.
Calif, Wiz and the web infrastructure company Cloudflare said the flaws affect PHP 5.4 and later versions, more than a decade of releases.
Cullen said the vulnerability was “really unprecedented”, noting that PHP powers more than 70 percent of websites globally, although sites that have been updated are protected.
“There is a real risk to the kind of shared digital infrastructure that we all rely on,” Cullen told Al Jazeera. “There is concern in the cybersecurity community about what the blast radius for this will be, even though the developers of PHP have been very quick to try and develop patches for it.”
Cullen added that while AI was getting better at cybersecurity, it was also getting better at being a hacker. “This means that we are developing systems … that are making the internet safer by helping to fix bugs, but we’re also making it riskier by discovering bugs and creating bugs they’ll be able to hack,” he said.
What has the impact been so far?
In the Netherlands, the Dutch cybersecurity agency itself went offline, saying it had done so as a precaution because of the vulnerabilities. Several organisations followed the example and took public-facing websites offline, including the Port of Rotterdam, government portal Overheid.nl, the national football association KNVB, the websites for the country’s five largest political parties and several hospital websites.
Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten said he was closely monitoring the situation.
Disruptions were even more widespread in Finland, where state IT services provider Valtori said government public network services had been taken offline “as a precautionary measure”.
France’s Ministry of the Interior said it had placed all of its websites into preventive maintenance.
Belgium’s Federal Public Service Foreign Affairs, Foreign Trade and Development Cooperation said it had temporarily taken its websites offline after reports of cyberattacks exploiting the PHP vulnerabilities although the country’s cybersecurity centre said it had not recorded any attacks on Belgian websites.
South Korea’s government raised its private-sector cybersecurity alert level and activated emergency response measures. It issued security guidance to about 28,000 companies with registered chief information security officers and 5,900 members of a government information-sharing network as well as operators of critical infrastructure, web-hosting firms and data centres.
The operator of the online encyclopedia Wikipedia also said it had taken down an unspecified number of systems until they could be safely patched while the Internet Archive, the sprawling online library, said it also briefly went offline to deal with the issue.

Poland Began Receiving Kleszcz Reconnaissance Vehicles to Replace BRDMs
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-22
12:32:18 UTC
21:32:18 KST

On October 21, the reconnaissance units of the Polish Armed Forces started receiving the first Kleszcz light armored reconnaissance vehicles.
These deliveries are the result of the implementation of the first agreement from August 2024 and will continue until 2028, with the next batch scheduled to arrive by the end of this year, according to the Polish Army’s website.
The project was launched by a framework agreement signed on February 28, 2024, between the Armaments Agency and AMZ-Kutno SA, which provides for the procurement of a total of 286 vehicles by 2035.
The first contract, worth $205 million, covers the delivery of 28 vehicles along with a package of logistical services, training, and investments in expanding production capacity.
The new armored vehicles are intended to completely replace several hundred obsolete Soviet BRDM-2 armored reconnaissance and patrol vehicles.
The Kleszcz (Bóbr-3) is a 4×4 amphibious armored vehicle developed between 2013 and 2022 by AMZ-Kutno SA in collaboration with Polish military research institutes.
Weighing 14–16 metric tons, the vehicle is equipped with a 326 k.s. diesel engine and an Allison automatic transmission, allowing it to reach speeds of up to 100 km/h on the highway and 7 km/h on water.
The vehicle’s ballistic protection meets Level 2a of the STANAG 4569 standard (protection against 7.62×39 mm rounds and a 6 kg explosive charge), with the option to install additional armor panels.
The crew consists of five members: a commander, a driver-mechanic, a reconnaissance and communications systems operator, a weapons operator, and an external equipment operator.
The primary armament is the Kongsberg Protector remotely controlled module, capable of mounting a large-caliber machine gun or an automatic grenade launcher.
As a reminder, Poland received a batch of CGR-080 guided missiles and CTM-290 ballistic missiles for the Homar-K multiple launch rocket systems.
The shipment included CGR-080 missiles with a range of up to 80 km, as well as CTM-290 ballistic missiles with a range of up to 290 km.

Naser Abdel-Aal, chairman of the Egyptian Alumni Association of Chinese Universities, called for closer cooperation between Egyptian and Chinese researchers in clean energy, artificial intelligence (AI), 5G, cross-border e-commerce, and cloud computing.
He said the association would further promote cooperation between universities and research institutions in both countries.
Wu Bin, president of the Academy for International Business Officials under China's Ministry of Commerce, highlighted human resources development as an important platform for sharing China's modernization experience and promoting common development.
China has launched tailored training programs for Egypt this year, covering new energy infrastructure, AI and digital technologies, Wu noted.
Lu Chunsheng, minister counselor at the Chinese Embassy in Egypt, encouraged Egyptians who have studied in China to promote cultural exchanges and welcomed more young Egyptians to study in China.
Mahmoud Eissa, who went to China in 2013 to pursue a doctoral degree at Harbin Institute of Technology, told Xinhua that studying in China had profoundly changed his way of thinking and outlook on life.
"In China, I was deeply influenced by the country's atmosphere of striving for excellence and taking an enterprising approach," Eissa said, adding that he now strives for the best in everything he does. ■

HELSINKI, Oct. 22 (Xinhua) -- Finnish telecommunications equipment maker Nokia reported on Thursday a 10-percent year-on-year increase in third-quarter net sales, driven by strong demand for artificial intelligence (AI) and cloud infrastructure.
According to its interim financial report, Nokia's net sales reached 5.15 billion euros (5.77 billion U.S. dollars) in the July-September period, up from 4.7 billion euros (5.26 billion U.S. dollars) a year earlier. On a constant currency basis, sales grew 9 percent.
Comparable operating profit rose 35 percent year-on-year to 605 million euros (677.42 million U.S. dollars), while reported operating profit declined 22 percent to 196 million euros (219.46 million U.S. dollars), reflecting higher restructuring and integration costs.
Growth was particularly strong in Nokia's Network Infrastructure division, where net sales increased 15 percent on a constant currency basis, led by a 43-percent increase in IP Networks and an 18-percent rise in Optical Networks.
The company said net sales to AI and cloud customers jumped 123 percent year-on-year, while order intake surged 118 percent, with new orders totaling 1.5 billion euros (1.68 billion U.S. dollars) during the quarter.
Nokia President and CEO Justin Hotard said the company expects its combined Optical and IP Networks businesses to grow between 25 percent and 30 percent in 2027, citing growing demand for AI infrastructure that is becoming "larger, more distributed and hyperconnected."
Hotard also noted that Nokia, together with T-Mobile and NVIDIA, had completed what the company described as the world's first AI radio access network (AI-RAN) call on a live operator network, marking progress toward commercial deployment of AI-powered mobile networks.
Nokia maintained its full-year 2026 outlook, forecasting comparable operating profit of between 2.1 billion and 2.6 billion euros (2.35 billion and 2.91 billion U.S. dollars).
Despite the stronger earnings, Nokia shares fell in Helsinki on Thursday, declining around 3 percent by midday, according to Finnish business daily Kauppalehti. The newspaper attributed the market reaction partly to weaker-than-expected cash flow. ■

Some estuarine fish may withstand warming oceans: study

20:30:08 CST

CANBERRA, Oct. 22 (Xinhua) -- Some estuarine fish may be able to withstand warmer ocean conditions expected under climate change because of their genetically determined resilience to temperature extremes, new research finds.
The study examined three economically important estuarine species, yellowfin bream, sand whiting and tarwhine, and found that they were "thermal generalists" capable of tolerating a broad range of temperatures, according to a statement released Thursday by Australia's Adelaide University.
Yellowfin bream and sand whiting were among the Australian east coast's most commonly caught inshore fish, making their ability to cope with warming estuaries important for coastal fisheries, according to the researchers.
While these estuarine fish can tolerate extreme conditions, climate change is already shifting marine species' distributions, with tropical fish moving further south as waters warm and reshaping local fisheries, researchers said. ■

The international community prefers not to address the fact that violence poses a permanent threat to food security and, as a result, to any humanitarian paradigm. For 2026, the WPF received less than half its funding and requires $450 million “to maintain critical operations in the occupied Palestinian territory over the next six months.”
WFP’s announcement broke down the consequences of its funding shortage. Out of 1.6 million Palestinians in Gaza, 1.1 million remain eligible for WFP’s services. Food rations have been but down by half. Hot meals have been reduced from 250,000 to 150,000, while Palestinians living in the vicinities of the Yellow Line can only receive one hot meal on alternate days. The WFP also reduced cash assistance to 75,000 families. Bakeries are, until now, still supported, however the aid only covers one third of the population reached by the bakeries. Unemployment in Gaza is over 80 per cent, and 1.4 million Palestinians are classified as experiencing acute food insecurity.
Meanwhile, for the fifth consecutive year, Israeli arms sales broke another record – from $14.8 billion in 2024 to $19.2 billion in 2025. This means that during the genocide in Gaza, when government were begrudgingly fulfilling their rhetorical duty calling for humanitarian pauses and deploring civilian deaths, arms sales were contributing to the genocide and, as a result food insecurity.
Governments have billions to spend on weapons while $450 million to maintain the WFP’s critical operations are hard to come by.
READ: UN: 950,000 displaced people in Gaza face flood risks this winter
Governments also support humanitarian paradigms, albeit only as a veneer against their complicity in fomenting violence. However, even that veneer can no longer support its own narrative, as the consequences of Israel’s internationally supported genocide in Gaza is further illustrating that humanitarian aid was never designed to be permanent. The budget allocated to humanitarian aid was never on a par with that allocated for war. With that discrepancy, it is likely that a state of permanent colonial violence in Gaza is fast becoming normalised to the point that the lack of humanitarian aid will go the same way.
Just as forced displacement no longer elicits anything but statistical data, so will humanitarian aid follow the same trajectory. Funding deficits are already normalised, and so will food insecurity and starvation.
Calling upon Israel to assume its responsibilities as an occupying power never worked. The humanitarian paradigm failed since its inception. The weakest calls from the international community are for Israel to exercise restraint, while the loudest silence encouraged genocide. It is only here that the international community’s warped logic shines through – it will not contradict its own complicity in genocide by investing more in the humanitarian paradigm. On the contrary, Gaza remains testimony to genocide and the international community’s commitment to it. If Israel and the international community do not carry the humanitarian burden because it contradicts their complicity in genocide, Palestinians then face permanent food insecurity. As things stand, all roads lead to genocide in Gaza, and Israel has already completed the groundwork with the international community’s aid.

====================================================================================================

Hong Kong’s Vanishing Rainbow Shows How China’s Social Control Travels
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-22
12:25:00 UTC
21:25:00 KST

China’s growing pressure on LGBTQ communities is increasingly transnational. Chinese nationals who attend Pride events overseas can attract police attention after returning home; overseas Chinese LGBTQ groups remain vulnerable to censorship on Chinese platforms; cultural spaces in Europe can lose access to Chinese social media for promoting transgender films; and mainland writers publishing gay fiction on overseas platforms have faced prosecution at home. Hong Kong offers a particularly revealing entry point because similar pressures are visible there even though same-sex relationships are legal (though not legally recognized as marriages).
In October, the organizing committee of Hong Kong Pride canceled its annual Rainbow Market at Central Market after being told that an administrative error had resulted in double-booking. Organizers had already received confirmation, paid a deposit, and announced the venue.
The cancellation followed a wider pattern. Earlier in 2026, Pink Dot HK, the city’s largest annual LGBTQ carnival, canceled its event after the operator of Stanley Plaza and Murray House withdrew the venues, citing unresolved licensing issues. It was the second consecutive year in which Pink Dot failed to proceed. In 2025, negotiations to hold the event at West Kowloon Cultural District’s Art Park had also collapsed.
Hong Kong Pride itself lost a planned venue at Kwun Tong Promenade in 2025 after organizers had already paid rent and announced the event.
These cases illustrate how LGBTQ public life in Hong Kong is being narrowed through administrative and institutional means rather than formal criminal prohibition. Consensual same-sex conduct remains legal, and LGBTQ organizations continue to exist. But these groups find it harder and harder to organize publicly, retain venues, sustain institutions, and remain visible in civic life.
This is striking because Hong Kong once had one of the most visible LGBTQ communities in East Asia. The city decriminalized consensual homosexual conduct between adult men in 1991, while its courts later expanded legal protections for same-sex couples in areas including immigration, taxation, and public housing. Social acceptance also rose significantly. Survey research published in 2023 found that 69 percent of respondents were “moderately” or “very accepting” of gay men and lesbians, while 60 percent supported same-sex marriage and 71 percent supported anti-discrimination legislation based on sexual orientation.
Hong Kong Pride once drew thousands into the streets, but its last full Pride march took place in 2018. In 2019, police declined permission for a march amid the citywide protests and permitted only a static rally. Pandemic restrictions later pushed Pride activities online, after which organizers shifted toward indoor markets and smaller events. The large public march never returned.
Most LGBTQ organizations in Hong Kong were never primarily political in the conventional sense. Their work focused on discrimination, health, family acceptance, culture, community support, and legal equality. Their shrinking space therefore shows how Hong Kong’s post-2020 transformation has moved beyond suppressing explicit political opposition and into regulating autonomous social life.
The same pattern is visible in mainland China. China decriminalized homosexuality in 1997 and removed homosexuality from its official classification of mental disorders in 2001 (in practice, if not in actual fact). During the 2000s and early 2010s, LGBTQ organizations, university groups, online communities, and cultural events expanded in major cities. Under Xi Jinping, that space has contracted sharply. Shanghai Pride ceased operations in 2020, the Beijing LGBT Center closed in 2023, university LGBTQ groups have faced mounting restrictions, and social media accounts associated with sexual minority organizations have been deleted or suspended.
Foreign connections have become increasingly important to this repression. Chinese authorities often treat independent organizations with international ties as possible channels of foreign influence. LGBTQ groups are especially exposed because contemporary sexual minority advocacy is highly transnational, involving foreign NGOs, embassies, academic institutions, cultural organizations, and legal networks. This allows questions of private identity and social equality to be reframed as questions of sovereignty and political security.
The reach of this logic now extends beyond China’s borders. In 2026, France’s Le Monde reported that Chinese nationals who had participated in Bangkok Pride later received police attention after returning to China. How the authorities identified them remains unclear, but participation in a lawful LGBTQ event in Thailand had become a matter of interest to Chinese police.
This fits within the broader discussion of transnational repression, but LGBTQ communities also reveal a related form of cross-border control that operates through information systems. Chinese platforms and censorship practices increasingly project domestic restrictions into overseas Chinese-speaking communities.
The Chinese Rainbow Network illustrates this problem. The organization operates overseas, yet material on its WeChat public account became inaccessible. Citizen Lab had already shown the structural basis for such control when it found that content exchanged between non-China-registered WeChat accounts could still be subjected to analysis for politically sensitive material. Overseas users can therefore remain inside an information environment shaped by the political requirements of the Chinese party-state.
Recent cases involving the LGBTQ community show how this extends to cultural expression. The Paris-based Chinese-language cultural space 8lithèque reportedly had its Xiaohongshu (RedNote) account banned after promoting a screening of a transgender-themed film. The event was taking place in France, but the organizers remained vulnerable to the content rules of a Chinese platform.
The Haitang Literature City prosecutions show another dimension of this expanding reach. Haitang, a Taiwan-based platform, became popular among mainland Chinese writers of danmei and boys’ love fiction, including sexually explicit material. Chinese authorities later summoned, detained, and prosecuted mainland writers who had published on the platform, citing China’s obscenity laws. The platform was outside mainland China, but the writers were not beyond the reach of Chinese law enforcement.
Taken together, these cases show how China’s control increasingly travels through people, platforms, and language communities. Whether joining a cultural space in Paris, a platform in Taiwan, a Pride parade in Bangkok, or a community organization in North America, Chinese citizens and Chinese-language communities remain exposed to censorship, surveillance, or coercive pressure originating from inside China.
Why should LGBTQ communities matter so much to the party-state?
One reason is autonomous organization. Community centers, university societies, legal aid groups, online networks, cultural organizations, and Pride events create horizontal ties among citizens outside structures supervised by the Communist Party. Chinese authorities have become increasingly suspicious of such organization across many fields, including labor rights, feminism, religion, public health, and environmental activism.
Sexual minority rights also raise broader questions about pluralism. The principle that individuals should retain dignity and rights even when they depart from majority social norms places limits on the authority of the state, family, and society over private identity.
Family structure adds another dimension. Under Xi Jinping, official discourse has placed growing emphasis on marriage, reproduction, family responsibility, and demographic duty. These themes have become more prominent as China confronts low fertility, population decline, delayed marriage, and rapid aging. Women are increasingly encouraged to marry and have children, while official rhetoric emphasizes “good family traditions” and reproductive responsibility.
LGBTQ identities sit uneasily within this model because they challenge the assumption that adult life should culminate in heterosexual marriage and biological reproduction. They also complicate fixed gender roles within the family.
These tensions acquire greater political significance because Xi has tied social order to the broader project of the “great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.” The Communist Party increasingly presents itself as a guardian of Chinese civilizational continuity and social morality.
This emphasis on tradition also represents a shift in the party’s own ideological history. The early People’s Republic was explicitly revolutionary in its approach to family hierarchy. The 1950 Marriage Law attacked arranged marriage, concubinage, male superiority, and other practices described as remnants of the feudal family system. Maoist discourse framed women’s emancipation as part of the destruction of inherited social hierarchy.
Mao-era China was never sexually liberal, but the contrast shows that the Communist Party’s current appeal to traditional family values is selective rather than timeless. During the revolutionary period, dismantling inherited hierarchies served the party’s claim to be creating a new society. Under Xi, family hierarchy, reproductive responsibility, and civilizational continuity serve a different political purpose by reinforcing social order and distinguishing Chinese values from supposedly foreign liberal influence.
LGBTQ communities therefore sit at the intersection of several Xi-era concerns: autonomous organization, minority rights, gender hierarchy, demographic policy, foreign influence, and individual autonomy.
Repression can be effective at weakening the organizational capacity of such groups. Authorities can close community centers, prevent events, delete accounts, restrict fundraising, discourage international partnerships, and make public participation more risky. But these measures cannot remove the identities and experiences that produced these communities.
That creates a long-term political problem. Concepts such as constitutionalism or representative government can remain abstract for citizens who encounter them mainly through rhetoric. Sexuality and gender are experienced through everyday life. Government policy reaches LGBTQ people through relationships, family formation, public expression, employment, access to community, and the ability to describe oneself openly. Feminists encounter a similar dynamic when state-defined expectations concerning marriage, reproduction, and gender roles collide with their own lives.
Repeated discrimination turns political authority into a personal experience. Not every LGBTQ person or feminist will become politically oppositional, but a state that continually restricts people at the level of identity, family, and bodily autonomy risks creating durable alienation that cannot easily be displaced by nationalism or civilizational rhetoric.
The contraction of LGBTQ space in Hong Kong therefore matters beyond sexual minority rights. It shows how the logic of political control can expand into social life and how Chinese digital platforms, information systems, and law enforcement practices can extend that control across borders.
For LGBTQ communities, the immediate result is the erosion of public and organizational space. For Beijing, the longer-term consequence may be a widening gap between its civilizational narrative and the everyday experience of those whose identities increasingly fall outside the social order it seeks to define.

Russia sentences 77-year-old Crimean political prisoner to 18 years over alleged plot to assassinate Kremlin-installed governor
Volodymyr Ananiev, a 77-year-old Crimean political prisoner, has been illegally sentenced to 18 years in prison by a court in Rostov-on-Don. Ananiev is accused of plotting an "assassination attempt" on Sergei Aksyonov, the so-called head of occupied Crimea.
Source: Crimean Tatar Resource Center
Details: Volodymyr Ananiev was detained in Simferopol on 2 February 2024 while he was at an acquaintance's flat.
Russian investigators claim that Ananiev was part of a group that used a hidden camera to monitor Sergei Aksyonov. The group was allegedly preparing a remotely controlled explosive device, which they stored in a rented garage in Simferopol.
Volodymyr Bodnar and Oksana Shevchenko are also implicated in the case. The Russian occupation authorities sentenced them earlier: Bodnar received 13 years in prison and Shevchenko 10 years.
The 77-year-old Ananiev was "tried" by the Southern District Military Court in Rostov-on-Don and sentenced to 18 years in prison. He will spend the first four years in prison and the remainder of his sentence in a maximum-security penal colony.
Ananiev was also ordered to pay a fine of RUB 600,000 (about US$7,300).
"Volodymyr Ananiev is the oldest Crimean political prisoner. He has problems with his eyesight, spine, muscles, kidneys and legs and walks with a cane. He has undergone surgery on both eyes, but his eyesight continues to deteriorate, and glaucoma is developing in one eye. He also suffers from high blood pressure," the Crimean Tatar Resource Center reported.
The centre added that 64 elderly Crimean political prisoners have faced persecution by Russia. Of these, 45 have already been sentenced and 19 are being held in pre-trial detention centres.
Background: Earlier, the condition of 68-year-old Halyna Bekhter from Zaporizhzhia Oblast deteriorated significantly while she was imprisoned in Russia. Bekhter was "sentenced" under Russian occupation for transferring money to support the Ukrainian military.

Nestlé corrects recycling claims on plastic bottles

Nestlé corrects recycling claims on plastic bottles
Swiss firm Nestlé along with Coca-Cola and Danone are amending their recycling claims on plastic bottles. This comes after discussions with the European Commission and EU consumer protection authorities.
The aim is to correct misleading statements regarding recyclability. According to a statement issued by the European Commission on Thursday, companies intend to replace statements on bottle labels such as “This bottle is made from 100% recycled plastic” with phrases such as “This bottle is 100% recycled. Excluding the cap and label”. Labels such as “Recycle me again” are also to be changed to “Recycle me”.
The European Commission and national authorities reviewed the revised claims and found them to be in line with EU consumer protection law. According to the Commission, Coca-Cola and Nestlé have already implemented some of their commitments, such as recycling pledges on digital channels.
+ Nestlé shamed as third-largest plastic polluter
The case was triggered in 2023 by a warning from the European consumer organisation BEUC, which targeted misleading recycling claims on plastic bottles. The European Commission and the national consumer protection authorities subsequently entered into dialogue with the companies.

Africa’s richest man expands fuel empire into Kenya

Africa’s richest man expands fuel empire into Kenya
Africa’s richest man Aliko Dangote has bought a roughly 25% stake in Kenya’s fuel pipeline operator as part of a wider push to expand petroleum distribution across the continent.
The Nigerian industrialist announced the acquisition at the Financial Times Africa Summit in London on Wednesday. Kenya Pipeline Company (KPC) operates pipelines and storage facilities supplying Kenya and other regional markets.
“We bought 25% of their pipeline network for the distribution of petroleum products,” Dangote said.
The purchase involved 4.5 billion KPC shares worth $335 million, bought at a slight premium to the last-traded price, the FT reported. Dangote said the acquisition and planned network expansion formed part of a continent-wide fuel distribution strategy. “We are going very aggressively with that,” he said.
Dangote also plans to invest $1.5 billion in expanding the pipeline network as part of a wider African refining, storage, and distribution business, the FT reported.
KPC operates about 1,342 km of pipelines transporting refined petroleum products inland from the port of Mombasa. Its infrastructure supports supplies to Uganda, Rwanda, Burundi, South Sudan, and eastern DR Congo.
Kenyan President William Ruto said on Tuesday that private investors had acquired a quarter of KPC from public entities, without identifying the buyers. The government sold a 65% stake through an IPO earlier this year to raise revenue, with the company listing on the Nairobi Securities Exchange in March.
The purchase follows the September 30 groundbreaking for Dangote’s planned 700,000-barrel-per-day refinery in Kenya’s coastal Lamu County. The project is intended to supply the wider East African market and is scheduled for completion in 2030.
Dangote already operates Africa’s largest refinery near Lagos, Nigeria’s commercial capital. The roughly $20 billion facility began commercial operations in 2024, helping the country reduce its reliance on imported fuel. In September, the company launched a $1.6 billion public offering to help finance an expansion intended to double its capacity to 1.4 million barrels per day.

“Badr Memorandum of Understanding” was signed between the Defense Ministries of Türkiye, Qatar, Indonesia, and Pakistan. (AA Photo)
The alliances Türkiye has recently joined with its regional allies demonstrate its rising influence and effective diplomacy, the Defense Ministry has said.
“Together with the Mecca Defense Alliance and the Badr Memorandum of Understanding, it is a concrete indicator of our country’s effectiveness and strategic cooperation in the international arena,” ministry officials said on Oct. 22.
The statement came after Türkiye, Qatar, Indonesia and Pakistan defense minister signed the Badr Memorandum of Understanding on Oct. 21 in Doha. Türkiye and Pakistan, along with Saudi Arabia, are also the members of the Mecca Defense Alliance set in early August.
“On the basis of mutual trust and common interests, we will continue our efforts toward reinforcing regional peace and security by establishing strong and sustainable partnerships with our complementary capabilities, capacities and experiences,” officials maintained.
The defense agreement signed between the four countries is a clear indication of strong friendship and the will to work together, they said.
“With this memorandum, it is aimed to establish long-term and sustainable strategic partnerships between our countries through the implementation of joint projects in the field of defense industry, the increase of research and development activities, the strengthening of infrastructure and supply chains, and the development of joint production capacity,” the officials said.
They also added that this agreement will contribute to peace and stability in the wider region.
Libya agreement fully legal
The officials also commented on the Libyan House of Representatives’ ratification of the Türkiye-Libya maritime delimitation agreement which was originally signed in late 2019.
Welcoming the parliamentary confirmation, the officials thanked Libyan officials who demonstrated a strong will to this end.
“We attach great importance on this memorandum, which contributes to protecting the rights and interests of both countries in the eastern Mediterranean. And we support the objective of a ‘united and integrated Libya’ that brings the east and west of Libya together around a common future,” they stressed.
On the statements from the EU and Greece which argued that the deal is null and void, the ministry recalled that the agreement was signed between the two countries based on international law and interests of the littoral countries.
“The delimitation of maritime jurisdiction areas falls within the scope of the sovereign rights of the relevant coastal states, and the legal validity of the said Memorandum of Understanding cannot be nullified by the unilateral assessments of third parties,” they noted.

Pentagon pledges to buy 850 F-35 jets under 10-year deal with Lockheed Martin
Unknown
Unknown Publisher

Berk Kutay Gokmen
22 October 2026•Update: 22 October 2026
The Pentagon has moved to purchase at total of 850 F-35 fighter jets from Lockheed Martin over the next 10 years, marking the longest commitment among recent Trump administration efforts to prepare suppliers for wartime production.
The new framework agreement, announced on Thursday, includes 850 F-35 Lightning II aircraft for the US military, hundreds more for international customers, as well as spare parts and other equipment.
The deal would secure the defense contractor’s plan to produce 156 jets each year in the coming years.
The Defense Department said Lockheed Martin had agreed to fund $7 billion in investments from its own resources to support the long-term production plan.
The agreement announced on Thursday is a step toward a final contract, which would require tens of billions of dollars in congressional funding to be finalized.
The stealth fighter program has already been described as the world’s most expensive weapons program, with projected lifetime costs of $2 trillion for purchasing, operating, and maintaining the aircraft.
Pentagon officials have said that firm, multiyear purchase commitments help make weapons procurement more efficient. Suppliers involved in military programs often complain that inconsistent congressional funding makes long-term planning difficult.
“This multiyear framework strengthens the way we can plan and invest in the F-35 enterprise,” said Lockheed Martin CEO Jim Taiclet.

Under the rules, platforms must reject registrations by children under 15 and close existing accounts found to belong to them. Users aged 15 to 17 will be subject to additional safeguards, including private accounts, restrictions on livestreaming and personalized advertising, and a ban on infinite-scrolling feeds.

Birds are more afraid of women than men. Scientists have no idea why
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-22
12:06:14 UTC
21:06:14 KST

Birds are more afraid of women than men. Scientists have no idea why
- Date:
- October 22, 2026
- Source:
- British Ecological Society
- Summary:
- Scientists have uncovered a strange pattern in urban bird behavior: Across five European countries and 37 species, birds consistently fled sooner when approached by women than men. Researchers have no clear explanation for the difference, raising intriguing questions about how birds recognize and respond to humans.
- Share:
Birds living in cities appear to react differently to men and women, and scientists are struggling to explain why. An international research team discovered that urban birds, including great tits, house sparrows, and blackbirds, tend to fly away sooner when approached by women than by men. The surprising behavior raises new questions about how birds perceive the people around them.
The study took place in five European countries, where male and female participants (matched for height and clothing) walked directly toward birds in city parks and other green spaces.
On average, men were able to approach about one meter closer than women before the birds flew away. The researchers measured this response by recording how close a person could get before a bird took flight (termed flight initiation distance).
Published in the British Ecological Society journal People and Nature, the findings showed the same pattern in Czechia, France, Germany, Poland, and Spain. The difference also appeared across all 37 bird species examined, including easily startled magpies and pigeons that typically allow people to approach much more closely.
Why Are Birds More Afraid of Women?
The researchers believe their findings indicate that city birds can distinguish between male and female humans. However, they have yet to determine which characteristics the birds recognize or why they appear more cautious around women.
Professor Daniel Blumstein of the University of California, Los Angeles, who helped conduct the research, said the results were convincing despite the lack of an explanation.
"I fully believe our results, that urban birds react differently based on the sex of the person approaching them, but I can't explain them right now. We used bleeding-edge comparative analysis techniques that showed our findings were consistent across cities and species, but we simply don't have a conclusive explanation yet."
Dr. Yanina Benedetti of the Czech University of Life Sciences Prague, another member of the research team, said the discovery challenged her expectations about how birds respond to human observers.
"As a woman in the field, I was surprised that birds reacted to us differently. This study highlights how animals in cities 'see' humans, which has implications for urban ecology and equality in science. Many behavioral studies assume that a human observer is neutral, but this wasn't the case for urban birds in our study."
What Are Birds Detecting in Humans?
Scientists have proposed several possible explanations for the difference. Birds might be responding to chemical signals such as pheromones, variations in body shape, or differences in how men and women walk. For now, however, these ideas remain speculative, and additional experiments will be needed to identify the actual cause.
Dr. Federico Morelli of the University of Turin, a co-author of the study, said the unanswered question is one of the discovery's most fascinating aspects.
"This is maybe the most interesting part of our study," said Dr. Federico Morelli from the University of Turin, a co-author of the study. "We have identified a phenomenon, but we really don't know why. However, what our results do highlight is the birds' sophisticated ability to evaluate their environment."
The findings suggest that urban birds may be sensitive to human characteristics that people themselves rarely notice. Identifying those signals could help researchers better understand how wildlife assesses potential threats in environments shared with humans.
Dr. Benedetti said: "Urban birds clearly react to subtle cues that humans do not easily notice. Follow-up studies could focus on individual factors such as movement patterns, scent cues, or physical traits, testing them separately rather than grouping them under observer sex. This approach would help identify the specific cues birds detect."
More Research Is Needed to Explain the Bird Behavior
Although the investigation included 2,701 observations, the researchers emphasize that their findings are still preliminary. Further studies will be necessary to establish whether the difference between birds' responses to men and women consistently appears in other settings and populations.
For now, the discovery points to an intriguing possibility: Birds sharing our cities may be paying attention to subtle differences between people that scientists have yet to fully understand.
Story Source:
Materials provided by British Ecological Society. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- Federico Morelli, Yanina Benedetti, Peter Mikula, Daniel T. Blumstein, Mario Díaz, Alicia Page, Piotr Tryjanowski, Marta K. Nowak, Eva Vincze, Gábor L. Lövei. Sex matters: European urban birds flee approaching women sooner than approaching men. People and Nature, 2025; 8 (2): 316 DOI: 10.1002/pan3.70226

Macron Moves to Ban “Illegitimate” Protests After France Riots
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-22
12:05:48 UTC
21:05:48 KST

French President Emmanuel Macron said Thursday that protests deemed “illegitimate” would be banned in the coming days, while organized groups such as unions would be offered alternative routes for marches to protect businesses, as authorities prepare for another nationwide wave of demonstrations following weekend riots and looting.
Macron made the announcement after meeting intelligence officials and senior ministers to discuss the crisis. He said a defense council meeting would take place Friday to decide on further measures ahead of Saturday’s protests.
“A defence council meeting will be convened tomorrow (Friday) under my chairmanship, and we will take further decisions,” Macron said, adding that only demonstrations organized by unions would be authorized nationwide on Saturday.
He blamed “seditious” ultra-left groups and vandals for last Saturday’s riots and looting across France. The government has also announced plans to deploy French soldiers on the streets.
Security forces planned for Saturday will be 20% more numerous than those deployed on October 17, Jean-Didier Berger of the Interior Ministry said on BFMTV.
“We are at a deployment level that is 20 percent higher than it was last week,” Berger said.
The operation will also involve soldiers from the Sentinelle anti-terrorism force, elite police and gendarmerie units including RAID, GIGN and BRI, as well as helicopters and armored vehicles. Around 60,000 police officers and gendarmes were deployed nationwide on October 17.
Authorities have imposed further restrictions on demonstrations. Police banned protests in parts of Paris on Thursday, with the restrictions in force from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. and covering key sites including the Élysée presidential palace, both houses of parliament, the Louvre museum and the Champs-Élysées.
The Paris restrictions were announced Wednesday, after Macron appeared to criticize U.S. President Donald Trump for using the unrest for political advantage in the U.S. midterm election campaign.
In Lyon, France’s third-largest city, officials have prohibited all demonstrations scheduled for Saturday. The Rhône prefecture said in a statement Thursday that the ban had been ordered in response to the events of October 17.
Police have also arrested a second suspect in connection with a fire that destroyed the Limoges town hall on Saturday. The public prosecutor’s office said a 66-year-old man was detained in La Creuse over suspected involvement in the incident. A man in his 30s arrested Tuesday has been charged with attempted murder of police officers who were inside the building when it was set on fire.
The unrest has prompted businesses to tighten security. Hermès has increased security at its stores in France after one of its boutiques in Marseille was looted, the luxury group’s chief financial officer, Eric du Halgouet, said.
“At present, it is too early to assess the impact on our shops’ business and, above all, on tourism,” du Halgouet told analysts while presenting the company’s third-quarter sales. He added that the Marseille store would not reopen “anytime soon.”
France Unbowed, the left-wing party known as LFI, plans to demand an apology and explanations from Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu during a meeting with political leaders Thursday, along with political responses to the public mobilization, according to a letter from party coordinator Manuel Bompard.
Lecornu is hosting representatives of political parties at Matignon alongside Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez, Justice Minister Gérald Darmanin and the heads of French intelligence and law enforcement services.
The letter, co-signed by Mathilde Panot, who leads the party’s parliamentary group, and Manon Aubry, head of its group in the European Parliament, holds Lecornu “totally responsible” for the chaos around Saturday’s demonstrations. It also accuses the government of seeking to shift blame by alleging that LFI was responsible for violence the party has consistently rejected.
The letter refers to reports published earlier this week by investigative news outlet Mediapart, which alleged that Lecornu’s government had pressured intelligence agencies to blame LFI for the unrest. The government has denied the allegation.
Other countries have issued travel warnings in response to the protests. Thailand has urged its citizens to postpone nonessential trips to parts of Europe affected by unrest, while Malaysia has warned its nationals about travel to France.
“Those travelling from Thailand to Europe must closely monitor the situation as it is changing rapidly and France remains a concern as the situation is still ongoing,” Thai Foreign Minister Sihasak Phungketkeow told reporters late Wednesday during a visit to Italy.
The Malaysian Embassy in Paris advised Malaysians in France on Sunday to remain vigilant and exercise caution. It said travel to France remained unrestricted but recommended postponing nonessential trips until the situation improved. China has also warned its citizens traveling to France to take safety precautions, state broadcaster CCTV reported Monday.
France is preparing for another weekend of demonstrations by high school students and the Yellow Vest movement. Paris police have prohibited a student protest planned for Thursday, citing the organizer’s “inability to prevent violence and vandalism,” a police source told AFP. Lecornu is also due to meet mayors of cities badly affected by the weekend riots, including Paris, Marseille and Lyon.

Nearly all coral reefs risk collapse in 50 years: IUCN

2026-10-22

Nearly all coral reefs risk collapse in 50 years: IUCN
- The IUCN says 96% of coral reef systems are “critically endangered”, with nearly all shallow-water reefs facing an “extremely high risk” of collapse by 2075.
- Climate change is the main threat, as warming seas drive bleaching. Overfishing, pollution, coastal development and storms also damage reefs.
- The IUCN says reefs are “not yet lost” and can recover. It calls for sharp emissions cuts, stronger protection and restoration, and more investment.
AI generated
YEREVAN, Armenia – Nearly all of the world’s shallow-water coral reefs face an “extremely high risk” of collapse by 2075 due to climate change, the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) warned on Oct 22.
In the first global assessment of its kind, the world authority on threatened wildlife classified 96% of the planet’s coral reef systems as “critically endangered” – its highest risk category.
Corals are heat sensitive and particularly vulnerable to human-driven climate change, which is warming the world’s oceans and increasing the frequency and intensity of damaging bleaching events.
“The future threat of climate change is looming and severe, and that poses a very high risk to the survival of these ecosystems,” said Mishal Gudka, scientific lead of the IUCN Red List of Coral Reef Ecosystems assessment.
The emergence in 2026 of a “super” El Nino, the natural warming phenomenon, also presents a risk to corals, Gudka said at a news conference at the United Nations’ COP17 biodiversity summit in Yerevan, Armenia.
The IUCN presented its findings at COP17, where governments are under pressure to make progress on a landmark pact to halt and reverse biodiversity loss by 2030.
For its assessment, IUCN used the “middle-of-the-road” scenario from the UN’s panel of climate experts that projects global temperatures rising 2.7 deg C above pre-industrial levels by 2100.
The world is on track for 2.6 deg C warming this century under current global commitments to cut planet-heating emissions, the UN warned on Oct 21.
“Heat stress from climate change is the single most consistent threat driving coral reef decline worldwide,” the IUCN said in a statement.
Overfishing is also hurting corals as certain herbivores and predators help control algae and maintain an ecological balance, the organisation said.
The overexploitation of parrotfish and other groupers threatens 63% of coral reef ecosystems.
Coastal development, pollution, tourism and more frequent storms are among other threats.
Critically endangered coral
The IUCN’s analysis examined 127 tropical and subtropical coral systems covering 188,362 sq km.
The world’s largest and most biodiverse coral reefs are among those classified as critically endangered – Australia’s Great Barrier Reef, the Coral Triangle in South-east Asia and the western Pacific, the Caribbean’s Mesoamerican Barrier Reef System, and the Red Sea coral reefs.
A reef ecosystem collapses when hard corals – which build its living foundation – largely disappear and are replaced by algae, rubble and sponges.
A study published in the journal Nature last week found that, by 2020, nearly half of coral species were at “elevated relative risk of extinction”, with climate change the main driver of this decline.
Despite its warning, the IUCN said coral reefs in most parts of the world “are not yet lost”.
If scientists look only at what has happened over the past 50 years, excluding future climate projections, 24% of coral reef ecosystems would be deemed critically endangered instead of 96%, the IUCN said.
“This gives us a critical window for action for us to scale up conservation efforts and climate action to prevent the worst outcomes from occurring,” said Gudka, who is also research director at Coastal Oceans Research and Development in the Indian Ocean East Africa, a conservation organisation.
“The actions we take over the next few years will determine what these ecosystems look like at the end of the century, whether they persist as we have known them, or whether they transform into a different ecosystem, which is worth less to both nature and people,” he said.
IUCN director-general Grethel Aguilar said it was “not too late to give coral reefs a chance to recover”.
“We know what is needed: ambitious emissions reductions, stronger protection and restoration efforts, and sustained investment in resilient coastal ecosystems and the communities that depend on them,” she said in a statement. AFP

Kids’ aggression appears to shape parents’ discipline more than the reverse, study finds
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-22
12:00:51 UTC
21:00:51 KST

Children’s aggressive behavior may contribute to parents becoming less consistent with discipline, rather than inconsistent discipline simply causing children to become more aggressive, according to research published in Nature Communications. The study also found that shared genes explained part of the link between inconsistent discipline and aggression, and all of the link between positive parenting and lower aggression.
Parenting and childhood aggression have long been linked. Parents who inconsistently enforce rules tend to have children with more aggressive behavior, while greater positive parenting, such as praising and positively engaging with children, is associated with less aggression. These findings can easily be interpreted as evidence that parenting produces differences in children’s behavior.
But families are more complicated. Children can affect their parents just as parents can affect their children. Biological parents and children also share genes, meaning some of the genetic factors associated with a parent’s behavior could be inherited by their children and influence the children’s behavior.
Led by Joanna K. Bright of King’s College London, the researchers addressed these problems using two genetically informative studies of children between about 4.5 and 8 years of age. Both studies used the same questionnaires to measure inconsistent discipline, positive parenting and child aggression, allowing the researchers to check whether the results held across different samples and methods.
The first drew on Norway’s Mother, Father and Child Cohort Study, using extended-family data involving 53,532 children born to 42,538 mothers, who reported on their parenting and their children’s behavior when the children were 5 years old. By comparing families with different degrees of genetic relatedness, including twins and their children, the researchers could estimate how much of the relationship between parenting and aggression was associated with shared genetics.
The second dataset came from the U.S. Early Growth and Development Study and contained 561 adoption triads, each made up of an adopted child, the adoptive parents and the birth parents. The children, 57% of whom were male, were adopted shortly after birth and assessed at ages 4.5, 6, 7 and 8. Because adoptive parents and children did not share genes, associations between their behaviors provided a way of examining environmental pathways without the complication of genes inherited from those parents.
The results suggested a more complicated relationship than parenting simply causing aggression. In the Norwegian study, the correlation between inconsistent discipline and child aggression was modest. About 47% of this association was attributed to shared genetic factors, while 53% remained after accounting for genetic transmission.
When the researchers investigated that remaining relationship, the evidence pointed from child to parent. The best-fitting model included a path from child aggression to inconsistent maternal discipline but no path from discipline to aggression. The adoption study showed a similar pattern: children’s aggression was linked to more inconsistent discipline at the same age and predicted more inconsistent discipline at later ages, while paths from mothers’ discipline to children’s aggression were not statistically significant.
Bright and colleagues concluded that “childhood aggression drives inconsistent parenting beyond shared genetic influences.”
Sensitivity analyses using fathers’ reports in the adoption study painted a somewhat different picture. When fathers reported on both their own parenting and their children’s behavior, inconsistent discipline and child aggression appeared to influence each other in both directions at the same time point, though not over longer periods. When one parent’s report of child aggression was paired with the other parent’s report of parenting, no significant links emerged, which the authors note could mean that relying on the same person to report both behaviors inflates associations.
Positive parenting produced another important finding. Although greater positive parenting was associated with lower aggression in the Norwegian sample, the researchers estimated that the association was completely explained by shared genetic influences. In the adoption sample, the models found no evidence that positive parenting and aggression influenced each other in either direction.
The results did not differ meaningfully between boys and girls. The authors suggest that clinicians should recognize that childhood aggression can contribute to inconsistent discipline, and that interventions focused only on encouraging consistent discipline may be insufficient.
Some limitations should be noted. The authors caution that their questionnaires captured relatively narrow aspects of parenting and aggression, relied primarily on mothers’ reports, and were drawn from relatively socioeconomically advantaged families. The two samples also used somewhat different versions of the aggression measure, which captured defiant behavior as well as physical aggression.
The Norwegian analysis was based on a single time point and could not account for the possibility that parents choose partners with similar traits. The data were also collected between roughly 10 and 23 years ago, and parenting norms may have shifted since then.
The study, “Triangulating evidence for genetic and environmental components of associations between parental behaviours and aggressive behaviour in children,” was authored by Joanna K. Bright, Yasmin I. Ahmadzadeh, Olakunle Oginni, Essi Viding, Leslie D. Leve, Jenae M. Neiderhiser, Daniel S. Shaw, Misaki N. Natsuaki, Jody M. Ganiban, Eivind Ystrom and Tom A. McAdams.
